title: VPC tenant-aware traffic steering and graceful degradation playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a tenant-aware traffic steering and graceful degradation strategy for Redwood Private VPC deployments. It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for ensuring availability and predictable latency for tenant workloads when parts of the private deployment or upstream dependencies are degraded.

Goals
- Keep tenant traffic serving with the highest possible fidelity while meeting SLOs.
- Provide deterministic escalation and automated remediation steps.
- Minimize cross-tenant impact through prioritized routing, quota enforcement, and model-variant fallbacks.
- Offer clear rollback and validation steps after recovery.

Scope
- Applies to Private (VPC) deployments managed by Redwood private control plane with local runtime nodes and optional hybrid control-plane peering.
- Covers: local zone impairment, GPU node pool degradation, KMS/API latency spikes, control-plane control-plane connectivity loss, and model-serving performance regressions.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific network or security runbooks; it is complementary and assumes required RBAC and network ACLs have been documented in the customer handoff.

Key concepts and primitives
1) Tenant profile (TP): metadata assigned at onboarding that includes priority tier (gold/silver/bronze), latency SLO, max concurrent sessions, and allowed fallback policies.
2) Route policy: per-tenant routing configuration expressed as weights and fallback chains (model variant → quantized variant → cached responses).
3) Circuit breaker: per-tenant and per-service short-circuit conditions to avoid cascading failures.
4) Graceful degradation window (GDW): a configurable time window (default 30s) during which steering/fallback decisions must be reversible to avoid flapping.
5) KV-prefix caching: tenant-scoped prefix caching to reduce cold-start/regeneration work.

Service-level targets and thresholds (examples)
- Latency (p95 generation): <= 150 ms for gold; <= 250 ms for silver; <= 500 ms for bronze.
- Error rate (5xx + model-failure): <= 0.5% for gold; <= 1% for silver; <= 3% for bronze.
- Degradation alert thresholds: 10% of gold tenants above p95 for >5 min triggers severity-2.

Topology and dataflow (summary)
- In-region serving clusters host tenant workloads in isolated namespaces with soft resource quotas and ephemeral pod pools for model-warmth.
- A local envoy-based ingress performs tenant-aware routing to node pools and applies token-level quotas and circuit-breakers.
- Smart-router control plane maintains routing tables with TTLs and allows horizontal reweighting across zones or model variants.

Routing policy example (YAML)
---
tenant_id: tenant-acme
priority: gold
routes:
  - name: primary-model
    weight: 80
    model: rdx-7b-v2
    timeout_ms: 2000
  - name: quant-fallback
    weight: 15
    model: rdx-7b-q4
    timeout_ms: 1200
  - name: cached-response
    weight: 5
    behavior: return_cached_prefix_or_stub
circuit_breakers:
  - condition: model_response_errors > 5% in 1m
    action: reduce_weight(primary-model, by_percent=50)
    gd_window_seconds: 30
---

Operational patterns
- Tiered reweighting: During partial outage, prefer reducing weight of the primary model for lower-priority tenants first, then shift traffic to quantized variants or cache.
- Local healing: If a node pool shows elevated GPU thermal throttling, route traffic to alternate pools in the same region before cross-region failover to minimize latency impact.
- KMS fallback: If KMS latencies exceed 500 ms for >2 minutes, switch to customer-approved local key cache for short-lived tokens (subject to audit windows).

Automated rules and SRE runbook
This section defines automated detection thresholds and step-by-step manual runbook actions.

Detection and initial triage (automated)
1) Alert fired: "tenant-p95-exceedance" for N tenants.
  - Query: per-tenant p95, error-rate, model-latency, and ingress drop rate.
2) Auto-score incident severity: compute weighted score by number of gold tenants affected and magnitude over SLO.
3) If score >= sev-2: trigger automated reweighting policy (scripted) and page on-call.

Automated remediation steps (safe-by-default)
1) For affected tenants, apply conditional reweighting: reduce primary-model weight by 40% for bronze, 20% for silver, 10% for gold.
2) Enable per-tenant caching for prefix keys with TTL 60s.
3) If error rate does not improve in GDW (30s), increase fallback weight to quantized variants.
4) Log actions and create a short-lived incident tag in traces for postmortem.

Manual runbook (when automation insufficient)
1) Identify scope: Run the admin query:
   ./rdxctl tenant-stats --region us-west-2 --filter "p95>250" --json | jq '.tenants[] | {id, tier, p95, err_rate}'
2) Validate model health: Check runtime node metrics and model-serving logs:
   kubectl -n rdx-serving logs deployment/rdx-model-7b --since=15m | egrep "(OOM|KV-ERR|latency)"
3) If node pool degraded: Rebalance weight to alternate in-region pools:
   rdxctl routing update --tenant tenant-acme --set-route-weight primary-model=50,quant-fallback=45,cached-response=5 --comment "manual rebalance due to node thermal"
4) If KMS errors are present:
   - Confirm with security if local key cache allowed. If allowed, flip flag: rdxctl kms toggle-local-cache --tenant tenant-acme --enable --expires-in 10m
5) If cross-region failover required: follow controlled failover procedure (see section Controlled cross-region failover).

Controlled cross-region failover
Purpose: minimize data-plane impact and honor tenant data residency constraints. Pre-reqs:
- Cross-region peering and cockpit are green.
- Customer allowlist for cross-region failover exists in tenant profile.
- Model artifacts are available in target region (or can be fetched within 5 min).

Steps:
1) Set region-level read-only mode for non-critical operations to reduce load: rdxctl region set-mode --region eu-west-1 --mode read-only --reason "failover prep"
2) Reweight traffic in 10% increments over GDW to the target region for gold tenants, monitoring p50/p95 and error rate after each increment.
3) Keep silver/bronze at local quantized variants and only move if gold stability achieved.
4) Once stable for 10 min, update global routing table as final commit.
5) Document the event and notify customer success for impacted tenants.

Rollback and post-recovery validation
- Rollback strategy: always reverse reweights in the opposite order they were applied. Maintain a short-lived (1 hour) sticky tag that prevents automation from re-applying a previously failed automated policy.
- Validation checklist:
  - p95 and error rate returned to SLO targets for all gold tenants for 20 consecutive minutes.
  - No model-variant regressions observed in sample prompt set for primary-model.
  - KMS latencies within baseline.
  - All temporary flags (e.g., local key cache) have been revoked or extended under documented approval.

Testing and drills
- Quarterly chaos tests: simulate a node pool thermal spike and validate automated reweighting and rollback.
- Smoke test scenarios to include: KMS latency spike, partial model-corruption (intentional return of bad logits), and control-plane partition.
- Test harness: use rdx-sim with tenant profile variations; maintain a baseline golden prompt-set to validate quality after fallback.

Operational governance and ownership
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments/platform-ops (pager: #infra-oncall).
- SRE on-call: triage and first-line mitigation.
- Applied ML: validate quality regressions and recommend model-variant thresholds.
- Security: approve and audit any KMS local-cache toggles.

Runbook appendix (commands and snippets)
- Query per-tenant latencies (example):
  rdxctl metrics query --name tenant_p95 --window 5m --filter "region=us-west-2" --output table
- Snapshot routing table:
  rdxctl routing snapshot --region us-west-2 --output json > /tmp/routing-snapshot-$(date +%s).json
- Force revert to snapshot:
  rdxctl routing restore --file /tmp/routing-snapshot-1678823456.json --dry-run=false --comment "revert after recovery"

Configuration checklist (for customer handoff)
| Item | Required | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Tenant profile (priority/tier) | yes | Must be set at onboarding
| Cross-region failover allowlist | optional | Must be explicit for GDPR/data-residency sensitive tenants
| KMS local-cache policy | optional | Requires Security approval and audit annotations
| Model artifact regional replication | recommended | Automate with artifact sync jobs to limit cross-region cold fetches
| Prefix-caching enabled | yes | Default TTL 60s, configurable per-tenant

Audit and compliance notes
- All automated reweighting actions are logged with an immutable audit id and must include the triggering alert id.
- Any KMS local-cache activation requires a ticket in the customer handoff tracker and a security reviewer sign-off.

Change history and references
- Created 2027-03-15 by Maya Chen.
- Reviewed and published 2028-01-10 after field validation with customer Acme Corp and bench tests.
- Related internal documents: reference architectures for regional model fallback, private deploy onboarding checklist, and the day-2 ops tenant isolation playbook.

Contact and escalation
- Platform owner: eng-private-deployments/platform-ops (platform-ops@redwood.com)
- SRE on-call: see #infra-oncall (internal chat)
- Security escalation: security@redwood.com (pager: #sec-oncall)

Appendix: sample incident timeline (example)
- 00:00 alert fires for 6 gold tenants. Automation reduces primary weight by 10% (auto).
- 00:01 on-call paged, automated cache enabled for affected tenants.
- 00:04 manual rebalance to alternate in-region pool after node pool telemetry shows GPU thermal alarms.
- 00:12 p95 improves and automation gradually restores weights; local key cache revoked at 00:20.
- 00:35 all metrics stable; rollback snapshot applied and incident closed.

End of document
